coverLetter.title: 자기소개서 Builder
coverLetter.subtitle: Create a compelling Korean self-introduction letter

guidance.growth: Share formative experiences that shaped you, with concrete examples of perseverance and growth.
guidance.personality: Be honest about strengths and weaknesses, and show self-awareness by explaining how you address a weakness.
guidance.motivation: Research the company and reference specific products, values, or initiatives that resonate with you.
guidance.aspiration: Be specific about your goals — concrete, realistic plans read better than vague ambition.
guidance.custom: Answer the company's question directly, using concrete examples, numbers, dates, and named events.

intro.title: Before you write
intro.subtitle: A few principles that apply to the whole self-introduction.

core-depth.title: Depth beats breadth
core-depth.body: Don’t list many experiences shallowly — analyse one deeply. A strong essay wins on interpretation, not on a list of events.

core-competency.title: Competency over identity
core-competency.body: Don’t lead with being “a foreigner.” It’s only a tool — your competency must be the centre of the essay.

growth-formula.title: One scene · 4-step formula (500 chars)
growth-formula.body:
Step 1 (10%): Pick one decisive scene — not your whole life, just one key moment.
Step 2 (30%): Describe when, where and what you did, so it’s easy to picture.
Step 3 (40%, most important): State the value it shaped in one sentence — “I am a ___ person.”
Step 4 (20%): Connect that value to the target role and the benefit to the company.

growth-example.title: Step 3 example
growth-example.body: e.g. “I’m someone who keeps looking for a way even after failing.” Write the Step-3 sentence, then link it to the role.

growth-mistakes.title: 4 mistakes to avoid
growth-mistakes.body:
1. Chronological list: opening with “I was born in 1998…” can read as dull to many recruiters — better to avoid.
2. Family clichés: it’s usually safer to avoid lines like “I grew up in a loving family,” bragging about parents, or religion/politics.
3. Listing events: analysing one experience deeply is usually more effective than five (exchange, internship, volunteering) shallowly.
4. Rather than repeating “because I’m a foreigner,” it’s recommended to keep identity as a tool and put competency at the centre.
※ Expectations can vary by company — check the job posting.

motivation-formula.title: Why us · why this role
motivation-formula.body:
A-axis (company): mention the firm’s recent news, new products or expansion. e.g. “Hearing your company plans to enter Southeast Asia in 2025…”.
B-axis (role): show which part of this job your past experience fits.
Tip for foreign applicants: add 2–3 sentences at the end on “why Korea, why this company.”

motivation-length.title: 500-char split
motivation-length.body: Split 500 characters as: 200 about the company + 200 about the role + 100 personal story.

whyKorea.warning: For foreign applicants, 'why Korea' is usually expected. Without it, employers may read a retention risk.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Koreer helps international applicants write Korean resumes (이력서) and self-introduction letters (자기소개서). This policy explains what we store, why we store it, and how you can remove it.

collect.account: Account: your email address and password (stored only as a hash we cannot read). If you sign up with a form, the name and country you enter; if you sign in with Google, the name, email and profile picture Google gives us.
collect.documents: Documents: everything you type into a resume or cover letter — including your name, phone number, address, date of birth, nationality, education, work history and, if you upload one, your photo. Photos are stored inside the document itself.
collect.profile: Career profile: the background, skills and "Why Korea" answers you save in Settings, so they can be reused across documents.
collect.technical: Technical: a sign-in token and your language choice, kept in your browser. We do not use advertising or analytics trackers.

use.b: Only to run the service: to sign you in, to store and show your documents, to produce PDF and Word files, and to generate the AI suggestions you ask for. We do not sell your data and we do not use it to train AI models.

ai.b: When you press an AI button, the text of that section — and the career profile you chose to save — is sent to Groq, our AI provider, to generate a suggestion. Nothing is sent unless you ask for it. AI output can be wrong: always check it before sending a document to an employer.

share.b: We use three providers, each only for the purpose listed. We do not share your data with anyone else.
share.supabase: Supabase — accounts and database (your documents and profile are stored here).
share.groq: Groq — generating AI suggestions when you request them.

retention.b: Your documents stay until you delete them. Your account and everything in it stay until you delete the account. Deleting the account removes your documents and profile permanently — there is no recovery.

rights.b: In Settings → Account you can change your password, download everything we hold about you as a JSON file, and delete your account. You can also delete individual documents at any time from your saved documents.

security.b: Every row in our database is protected by row-level security, so a signed-in user can only ever read and write their own data. Traffic is encrypted in transit. No system is perfectly secure, so please avoid putting information in a document that you would not want stored.

children.b: Koreer is intended for job seekers and students of working age. We do not knowingly collect data from children under 14.

changes.b: If we change how data is handled, we will update this page and the date above.

contact.b: Questions about your data, or a request to delete it, can be sent to:

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.intro: By using Koreer you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the service.

service.b: Koreer is a tool for writing Korean resumes and self-introduction letters, with optional AI assistance. It is a writing tool — it is not a recruitment agency, an employer, an immigration adviser, or a legal service.

account.b: You are responsible for keeping your password safe and for what happens under your account. Give an email address you actually control — it is the only way to reset your password.

acceptable.b: Do not use Koreer to write documents for someone else without their knowledge, to enter another person's data, to submit false information to employers, or to attack or overload the service.

content.b: You keep full ownership of everything you write. We store it only to provide the service and never publish it. We claim no rights over your documents.

ai.b: AI output is a draft, not a fact. It can be inaccurate or inappropriate for a specific company. You are responsible for checking every document before you send it. Anything Koreer says about hiring practices, visas or Korean law is general information — verify it with an official source. Using Koreer does not guarantee an interview or a job.

availability.b: The service is provided as is. We may change or pause features, and we cannot promise it will always be available or error-free. Export your important documents so you always have your own copy.

termination.b: You can delete your account at any time in Settings → Account. We may suspend an account that breaks these terms.

liability.b: To the extent the law allows, Koreer is not liable for hiring outcomes, lost opportunities, or damages arising from use of the service.

changes.b: If these terms change, this page and the date above are updated. Continuing to use Koreer means you accept the updated terms.
